title.en: Past simple: regular and irregular verbs
title.es: Past simple: verbos regulares e irregulares

summary.en: Use the **past simple** for finished actions at a time in the past: _We visited Rome last year. I bought a new phone on Saturday._ Regular verbs add **-ed**; irregular verbs have their own form (_go → went, see → saw_). Questions and negatives use **did / didn't** + base verb: _Did you see it? I didn't see it._
summary.es: Se usa para acciones terminadas en el pasado. Los regulares llevan -ed; los irregulares hay que aprenderlos. En preguntas y negativas, did/didn't + verbo base (sin -ed).

form: **Regular verbs**: base + **-ed** (_work → worked_); only **-d** after e (_like → liked_); consonant + y becomes **-ied** (_study → studied_); double the last letter after a short vowel (_stop → stopped_).
**Irregular verbs**: learn the form: _go → went, see → saw, have → had, make → made, take → took, buy → bought, get → got, come → came, eat → ate_.
Questions: **Did** + subject + base verb: _Did you call her? What did he say?_
Negatives: **didn't** + base verb: _I didn't go. They didn't answer._

uses.text: **A finished action at a stated time** → _I phoned her yesterday. We moved here in 2018._
**A series of past actions** → _He got up, had a shower and left the house._
**How long ago** → _I finished the course two weeks ago._

note.en: Time words: yesterday, last week, in May, three years ago.
note.es: Palabras típicas: yesterday, last week, in May, three years ago.

uses.text: **With yesterday, last… or ago, always use the past simple.**

note.en: Spanish can use a perfect form here; English cannot.
note.es: En español dices «ayer he visto»; en inglés, con yesterday, solo past simple.

mistakes.wrong: I goed to Madrid last week.
mistakes.right: I went to Madrid last week.

why.en: Go is irregular. Its past form is went.
After did the verb returns to the base form.
why.es: Después de did, verbo base: see.

why.en: After didn't use the base verb; the past is already in didn't.
why.es: El pasado ya está en didn't; el verbo va en base.

mistakes.wrong: Yesterday I have seen a good film.
mistakes.right: Yesterday I saw a good film.

why.en: With yesterday use the past simple, not have + participle.
why.es: Con yesterday no se usa have + participio.

why.en: Change y to i before -ed after a consonant.
why.es: Consonante + y: la y cambia a i antes de -ed.

examples.en: We arrived at the hotel just after midnight.
examples.es: Llegamos al hotel justo después de medianoche.

examples.en: I lost my wallet on the bus yesterday.
examples.es: Ayer perdí la cartera en el autobús.

examples.en: She studied biology at a university in Scotland.
Did you enjoy the concert? Yes, we had a great time.
examples.es: ¿Te gustó el concierto? Sí, lo pasamos genial.

examples.en: I didn't sleep well last night.
They stopped the car and asked for directions.
He wrote the report in two days and sent it to the manager.
We didn't buy anything because the shops were closed.
When did you meet your partner?

practice.prompt: I ___ a delicious pizza for dinner last night.

explanation.en: Eat is irregular. Its past form is ate.

practice.prompt: ___ you call your parents on Sunday?

explanation.en: A question about a finished action in the past starts with did.

practice.prompt: They didn't ___ the news until the next day.

explanation.en: After didn't the verb stays in the base form.

practice.prompt: The film ___ at eight and finished at ten.

explanation.en: A finished event in the past needs the -ed form.
